exposure: umbilical cord blood gas studies (UCGS) (pH groups and base excess)
cohort: The study included 14,338 low-risk deliveries that occurred between 2014 and 2022.
finding: Umbilical cord blood gas studies (UCGS) were an uncommon finding in low-risk deliveries, and their association with composite adverse neonatal outcome (CANO) was not clinically relevant, suggesting routine use should be reconsidered.
